nfl-2007-11-25-sf-ari: An eight-game losing streak ended in one of the wildest finishes of the 2007 NFL season as San Francisco beat Arizona 37–31 in overtime. [[espn:8479|Frank Gore]] powered the 49ers with 116 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 21 carries, plus 11 receptions for 98 yards. Across the field, [[espn:1682|Kurt Warner]] threw for 484 yards and two touchdowns, both to [[espn:5528|Larry Fitzgerald]], who caught nine passes for 156 yards.

The lead changed repeatedly. [[espn:649|Trent Dilfer]] connected with [[espn:4655|Arnaz Battle]] for a 57-yard third-quarter touchdown, but Arizona reclaimed the advantage in the fourth. Gore broke free for a 35-yard touchdown with 1:15 remaining to put San Francisco up 31–28. Warner marched Arizona downfield in the closing seconds, and [[espn:2300|Neil Rackers]] kicked a 19-yard field goal as regulation expired to force overtime.

Arizona nearly won it after Warner found [[espn:1994|Sean Morey]] for 62 yards, but a delay-of-game penalty preceded Rackers' missed 32-yard field-goal attempt. A punt and penalty later backed the Cardinals up to their own three. [[espn:8551|Ronald Fields]] sacked Warner in the end zone and forced a fumble that [[espn:4697|Tully Banta-Cain]] recovered for the walk-off touchdown. San Francisco swept its season series against Arizona and finally broke through after eight straight losses.
nfl-2008-12-07-stl-ari: Arizona's 34–10 victory over St. Louis delivered something the franchise had waited 33 years to celebrate: a division championship. The Cardinals clinched the NFC West and their first playoff berth since 1998, with [[espn:1682|Kurt Warner]] completing 24 of 33 passes for 279 yards against his former team. [[espn:11383|Tim Hightower]] opened the scoring with a one-yard touchdown run, and Warner found [[espn:5528|Larry Fitzgerald]] for a 12-yard touchdown as Arizona jumped ahead 14–0.

The Rams briefly answered when [[espn:2299|Marc Bulger]] connected with [[espn:5549|Steven Jackson]] for a three-yard touchdown, but [[espn:2300|Neil Rackers]] added field goals from 44 and 22 yards to make it 20–7 at halftime. [[espn:10585|Steve Breaston]] led Arizona receivers with seven catches for 90 yards, and Fitzgerald finished with six receptions for 73.

The Arizona defense turned the celebration into a rout. After a forced fumble, [[espn:5589|Darnell Dockett]] returned a loose ball 11 yards for a third-quarter touchdown. Rookie [[espn:11250|Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie]] then raced 99 yards with a fourth-quarter interception for another defensive score. The two defensive touchdowns sealed the Cardinals' first division crown since 1975 and a rare home postseason game for the franchise.
nfl-2023-12-03-ind-ten: Indianapolis outlasted Tennessee 31–28 in overtime at Nissan Stadium, turning a 17–7 first-half deficit into a fourth straight victory in a game shaped by special-teams chaos. [[espn:3043078|Derrick Henry]] powered the Titans with 102 rushing yards and two touchdowns, but [[espn:4038524|Gardner Minshew II]] answered with 312 passing yards and two scores. [[espn:4360078|Alec Pierce]] caught a 36-yard touchdown in the opening quarter and finished with three receptions for 100 yards.

The Colts' comeback hinged on two disrupted punts. [[espn:4426403|Nick Cross]] blocked a third-quarter attempt, and [[espn:4240255|Grant Stuard]] returned it 18 yards for a touchdown. On the ensuing two-point try, [[espn:4036134|Amani Hooker]] intercepted the pass and ran it back for two Tennessee points. Another punt disruption by [[espn:3115308|Tony Brown II]] set up a [[espn:4249087|Matt Gay]] field goal. The Titans rallied when [[espn:4361418|Will Levis]] found [[espn:15795|DeAndre Hopkins]] for a three-yard touchdown, but [[espn:10621|Nick Folk]] missed the extra point that would have given Tennessee the lead, leaving the score tied 25–25.

Folk put Tennessee ahead 28–25 with a 46-yard overtime field goal, forcing Indianapolis to respond with a touchdown. Minshew connected with Pierce for 55 yards to reach the four-yard line, then found [[espn:4035687|Michael Pittman Jr.]] for the winning score with 2:31 left. Pittman finished with 11 catches for 105 yards, and Indianapolis escaped with a crucial AFC South road victory.
